text:
Asha (PM): Quick sync: drafting Q4 roadmap slice for long-term platform routing. Goal: pick scope for a pilot around 'isolation corridors' (soft vs hard tenant isolation + geo routing). Need launch criteria and customer asks to commit.
Diego (Eng): +1. propose 3 deliverables: policy DSL v1, runtime routing hooks, and a rollout playbook.
Maya (Arch): Also need a model-compatibility matrix (quantization/variants) so canaries don't break.
Liam (SRE): Operational musts: evacuation flow, soft-evict, and cross-region failover SLOs. Oncall will gate launch without those.
Sophie (Sales): Customer asks: data residency and predictable p95 latency. Enterprise customers want region pinning in contract.
Jules (Customer Success): Add per-tenant burst caps and deterministic throttling requests from customers.
Asha (PM): Proposal: ship B-path (soft-isolation with QoS) as Q4 pilot, defer hard per-tenant dedicated lanes to enterprise A-path in Q1. Can we list launch gates?
Diego (Eng): Draft gates:
- policy DSL v1: region, affinity, fallback
- runtime: route by tenant tag + model family
- canary: safe fallback to compatible variant
- infra: tenant-level cache invalidation
- perf: perf regression <5% p50, p95 within targets
Maya (Arch): Add telemetry hooks (per-route tracing, token cost) and migration plan for tenants.
Liam (SRE): Ops gates: evacuation playbook, cross-region runbook, automated chaos test passed.
Sophie (Sales): Market gate: pilot customer signed with legal ok for region pinning + SLA appendix and pricing for reserved lanes.
Jules (Customer Success): Require migration checklist and two runbooks for customers + training session.
Asha (PM): Tradeoffs: per-tenant dedicated lanes = higher cost/complexity. Soft-isolation (B) = faster, uses runtime QoS and batching. Thoughts?
Diego (Eng): A increases bin-packing complexity and infra cost. B is faster and likely sufficient for many customers.
Maya (Arch): Dual-path recommended: ship B broadly, keep A as premium offering for regulated customers.
Liam (SRE): Agree, but ensure safe fallback semantics when switching between A and B to avoid data leakage — document in playbook.
Sophie (Sales): Maps to GTM: B = self-serve + standard pricing; A = enterprise + onboarding.
Asha (PM): Dependencies?
Diego (Eng): Kernel work for affinity routing, policy DSL parser + stable protobufs, runtime metrics plumbing.
Maya (Arch): Model registry needs flags for compatible fallback variants.
Liam (SRE): Networking for VPC pinning and KMS acceptance tests for Private mode.
Asha (PM): Timeline: if we scope to B-only, can Eng deliver an alpha by EoQ?
Diego (Eng): Yes if scoped: ~6 weeks DSL, 4 weeks runtime wiring, 2 weeks canary infra. Feasible.
Maya (Arch): I'll own compatibility matrix and model-registry changes.
Liam (SRE): I'll draft evacuation playbook and chaos tests.
Sophie (Sales): I'll line up two pilot customers: one mid-market (latency-focused) and one enterprise (wants roadmap for A).
Jules (Customer Success): I'll prep migration checklist and FAQ.
Asha (PM): Action owners + due: Q4 EoQ alpha (B-path). Escalate blockers if needed.
- Diego: policy DSL v1, runtime hooks
- Maya: telemetry + compatibility matrix
- Liam: evacuation runbook + chaos tests
- Sophie: pilot commitments
- Jules: migration & onboarding docs
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: infra/telemetry-proto bump -> 1750004350 :rocket: (automated)
Asha (PM): SLA for pilot suggestions?
Liam (SRE): Pilot SLA proposal: in-region p50 < 40ms, in-region p95 < 220ms, cross-region p95 < 450ms, availability 99.9% for dedicated lanes.
Sophie (Sales): Marketable; will confirm pricing with finance.
Diego (Eng): We'll capture token-level latency and cost before pilot; need billing accuracy for reserved lanes.
Maya (Arch): Note on fallback semantics: fallback variants must preserve input privacy and deterministic degradation.
Asha (PM): I'll turn this into a short PRD and launch checklist. Weekly syncs. :spiral_calendar:
